name: Yibbum (Levirate Marriage)
notes: Detailed laws of levirate marriage: who is obligated, how it is performed, acquisition of the yevama, and cases where it is inapplicable

name: Tzarat Ervah (Rival Wife of Forbidden Relative)
notes: Exemption of rival wife from levirate marriage when the other wife is a forbidden relative of the yavam; chain of rival wives of rival wives

name: Ḥalitza — Procedural Details
notes: Detailed laws of ḥalitza: the shoe, the court of three, the text recited, spitting, validity of ḥalitza under various conditions, night, left foot, missing limbs

name: Ma'amar (Levirate Betrothal)
notes: Rabbinic act of betrothal by a yavam to a yevama; effect on requiring a get in addition to chalitzah; distinction from full levirate marriage

name: Fifteen Forbidden Relatives Exempt from Yibbum
notes: The fifteen categories of women who are forbidden to the yavam as close relatives and are therefore exempt from both yibbum and chalitzah

name: Aylonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
notes: A woman incapable of bearing children due to developmental conditions; her effect on marriage, levirate marriage, teruma, and priestly marriage

name: Saris (Eunuch)
notes: Distinction between saris chamah (congenital eunuch) and saris adam (castrated eunuch); their obligations in chalitzah, levirate marriage, and marital law

name: Petzua Dakka and Kerut Shofkha (Genital Injuries Prohibiting Marriage)
notes: Men with crushed testicles or severed penis who are prohibited from marrying women born Jewish; their status regarding teruma and marriage

name: Entering the Congregation (Issur Kahal)
notes: Prohibition of Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, Edomites, mamzerim, Gibeonites, petzua dakka, and kerut shofkha from marrying into the congregation of Israel

name: Gibeonites (Netinin)
notes: Gibeonites who converted in Joshua's time; their prohibition from entering the congregation and marrying Jews of unflawed lineage, eternally

name: Testimony of Wife Regarding Husband's Death for Remarriage
notes: Special rules permitting a woman to testify about her husband's death to allow remarriage; one witness; hearsay; testimony of women, slaves, and gentiles; credibility standards

name: Woman Who Remarried Based on False Testimony
hebrew: אִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד שֶׁבַּעְלָהּ מֵת
notes: Laws governing a woman who remarried based on testimony that her husband died, and her husband later returned; she must leave both husbands, offspring is mamzer, various penalties

name: Sequence of Ma'amar, Get, and Ḥalitza in Levirate Situations
notes: What actions are effective or ineffective after prior acts by the yavam: get after get, ma'amar after ma'amar, intercourse, ḥalitza; the debate between Rabban Gamliel and the Rabbis

name: Eligibility to Eat Teruma Based on Marital Status
notes: When an Israelite woman married to a priest may eat teruma; disqualification through forbidden unions; effects of pregnancy, children, betrothal, and yibbum bond on teruma rights

name: Ḥalal and Ḥalala (Disqualified Priestly Lineage)
notes: Status of children born of forbidden priestly unions; disqualification from priestly privileges and teruma; how a woman becomes a ḥalala through intercourse with a disqualified priest

name: Mamzer Offspring from Forbidden Relations
notes: Definition of mamzer: dispute between Rabbi Akiva, Shimon HaTimni, Rabbi Yehoshua — whether it arises from any prohibition, karet-level, or capital-level forbidden relations

name: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel Dispute on Rival Wives
hebrew: מַחְלֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּצָרוֹת
notes: The fundamental dispute between Beit Shammai (permitting rival wives for levirate marriage) and Beit Hillel (forbidding them); practical consequences; their practice of intermarriage despite the dispute

name: Testimony on Order of Deaths for Levirate Exemption
hebrew: עֵדוּת עַל סֵדֶר מִיתוֹת לְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם
notes: Cases where a woman testifies about whether her husband or child died first; presumptive status and its effect on the credibility of testimony regarding yibbum obligation

name: Mi'un (Refusal of a Minor Girl to Continue Her Marriage)
notes: Rabbinic institution allowing a minor girl married by her mother or brothers to refuse her husband; effect on levirate marriage, disqualification from priesthood, repeat refusals; Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute

name: Mixed Offspring (Offspring of Uncertain Patrilineage)
notes: Cases where children's lineage is uncertain due to mixing; rules for chalitzah and levirate marriage; status for teruma, Temple service, inheritance, and priestly purity

name: Converts: No Levirate Bond Between Brothers
notes: Sons who converted with their mother are not considered brothers for purposes of levirate marriage or chalitzah; conversion is like rebirth

name: Three-Month Waiting Period Before Remarriage
notes: Requirement for widows and divorcées to wait three months before remarrying in order to establish paternity; who is included; exceptions; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei

name: Fulfillment and Details of the Mitzva of Procreation
notes: Number of children required; Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel; ten-year waiting period before divorcing an infertile wife; whether women are obligated

name: High Priest's Marriage Restrictions
notes: High Priest may not marry a widow, divorcée, ḥalutza, or grown woman (bogeret); may only marry a virgin; betrothal before appointment; High Priest must perform chalitzah not yibbum

name: Disqualification of Kohen's Wife from Teruma by Intercourse
notes: How forbidden intercourse or betrothal to prohibited men disqualifies a priest's wife from eating teruma; betrothal vs. marriage for this purpose; dispute between Rabbi Elazar/Shimon and the Sages

name: Falling into Water — Testimony of Death
notes: When a man falls into water, rules about testifying to his death; distinction between water with visible end and without visible end; cases from tradition

name: Identification of the Dead (Partzuf and Simanim)
notes: Requirement to identify a corpse by the facial features (partzuf); three-day limit; inadequacy of bodily marks or belongings alone for testimony permitting remarriage

name: Relying on a Disembodied Voice (Bat Kol) for Permitting Remarriage
notes: Unusual leniency of relying on a disembodied voice as evidence of a husband's death; specific cases cited in the Mishnah

name: Single Witness Testifying to Husband's Death
notes: Special rabbinic leniency allowing a woman to remarry based on one witness testifying to her husband's death; tradition from Rabban Gamliel the Elder; inclusion of women, slaves, hearsay

name: Rival Wife's Testimony — Inadmissibility
notes: Five categories of women not deemed credible to testify about each other's husbands' deaths due to conflicts of interest: rival wife, mother-in-law, stepdaughter, daughter of mother-in-law, yavam's wife

name: Prohibition of Ammonite and Moabite Converts
notes: Ammonite and Moabite males are prohibited from marrying into the Jewish people eternally; their females are permitted immediately; distinction from Egyptian and Edomite converts

name: Wife of a Brother With Whom He Did Not Coexist
notes: A brother born after the first brother's death has no levirate bond with the first brother's widow; the exemption of the wife of a brother who predeceased the yavam's birth

name: Zikah (Levirate Bond)
notes: The halakhic bond between a widow and her surviving brother-in-law (yavam) prior to yibbum or chalitzah; its effects on remarriage, teruma, and rival wives

name: Ketubah of a Yevama
notes: The yevama's marriage contract rights: payable from first husband's estate; property rights during the waiting period; Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute on inheritance if she dies

name: Yavam's Inheritance of Deceased Brother's Estate
notes: Whether a yavam who consummates levirate marriage acquires his brother's estate solely, or shares equally with other brothers; dispute including Rabbi Yehuda's view about the father's priority
